operation: Exact-tag Apache Kafka 4.2.0 cross-check of the message generator's flexible variable-length encoding rule against ListTransactionsResponse schema arrays.

sources.observed: generateVariableLengthReader selects readUnsignedVarint() - 1 when fieldFlexibleVersions contains the active version; generateVariableLengthWriter selects writeUnsignedVarint(length + 1) for flexible versions.
ListTransactionsResponse validVersions are 0-2, flexibleVersions are 0+, and both UnknownStateFilters ([]string) and TransactionStates ([]TransactionState) are present in versions 0+.

finding: Within Kafka tag 4.2.0, the generator source maps flexible-version variable-length fields, including arrays, to compact length encoding: readers subtract one from an unsigned-varint length and writers emit length plus one as an unsigned varint. Because ListTransactionsResponse declares all supported versions flexible and both top-level array fields present in all versions, this generator rule applies to those two array lengths for versions 0-2. Therefore an empty array's encoded length prefix is unsigned-varint 1 under this generator path. This closes the FE-519 generator-mapping source gap but does not by itself demonstrate a serializer bug, wire incompatibility, or runtime failure.
